ledger.sentence: On 23 September 2026 the WHO published guidelines on expanding contraceptive options, covering extended pill use, longer implant use and an extra emergency option.
ledger.note: Search 2/23: release dated 23 Sep 2026 with 'WHO guidelines on expanding contraceptive options'; pills extended; implants up to five years; mifepristone additional emergency option.

ledger.sentence: The WHO released its guidelines on expanding contraceptive options on 23 September 2026.
The guidelines support extended use of combined oral contraceptive pills as an alternative to cyclical use.
ledger.note: Search 23: 'combined oral contraceptive pills can be taken for extended periods'.

ledger.sentence: They also support longer use of contraceptive implants and add mifepristone as an emergency contraception option.
ledger.note: Search 23: implants up to five years; mifepristone additional option.

ledger.sentence: The WHO recommends against adding quinestrol-containing contraceptive pills to national programmes.
The World Health Organization (WHO) published "WHO guidelines on expanding contraceptive options" on 23 September 2026.
ledger.note: Search 23: release accompanies new publication of that title.

ledger.sentence: The WHO now supports extended use of combined oral contraceptive pills as an alternative to cyclical use, and longer use of contraceptive implants, which it says may reduce the need for replacement procedures, clinic visits and costs.
ledger.note: Search 23: extended periods; implants up to five years (potentially reducing the need for replacement procedures, clinic visits and associated costs).

ledger.sentence: Mifepristone is recommended as an additional emergency contraception option.

The WHO recommends against adding quinestrol-containing contraceptive pills to national contraceptive programmes, and says more research is needed on ormeloxifene before it enters family planning programmes.
ledger.note: Search 23 and Search 2 (limited evidence and reports of serious adverse events).

ledger.sentence: The WHO also announced its first Target Product Profile for male contraceptive methods, which sets out what such products would need to achieve.
ledger.note: Search 23: 'first Target Product Profile for male methods'. The gloss 'sets out what such products would need to achieve' is a plain definition, textbook. [second pass: edited to supported correction: News item says WHO developed its first Target Product Profile for male contraceptives (safety, effectiveness, acceptability, affordability). Document ]

ledger.sentence: The WHO frames the new guidelines as widening the safe options available to people choosing a method.
ledger.note: Search 23: release title 'expands safe options for contraception'.
